decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-3/4 to 2 percent.

changes.quote: economic activity has been rising at a strong rate
changes.explanation: The Fed upgraded its description of economic activity from a solid rate to a strong rate.

changes.quote: the unemployment rate has stayed low
changes.explanation: Instead of noting a recent decline, the Fed points out that the jobless rate is remaining low.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly
changes.explanation: The Fed removed the phrase about spending picking up and simplified the view to strong growth overall.

changes.quote: overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent
changes.explanation: The Fed changed its phrasing from inflation having moved close to 2 percent to staying near 2 percent.

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-3/4 to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Committee shifted its action from raising rates at the prior meeting to holding them steady at this meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a strong rate.
Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.63% APR costs about $56.79 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.52% would rise by about $7.15 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4%, and employers added an average of 227k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.8% over the past year (June 2018); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.1%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.14% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee will continue assessing economic data relative to its employment and inflation goals to decide future rate moves. As an educational note, a forecast model estimates a 62% chance of a hold and a 38% chance of a hike at the next meeting.
